answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a scarce, verifiable history of completed work that cannot be bought in bulk: every agent starts with a small spending cap and earns a higher cap only by finishing real tasks whose results are checked by unrelated peers. Like quartz forming slowly under pressure, reputation should crystallise gradually, not appear overnight. A sybil farm facing an ocean of required honest jobs, with each fake buffeted by the gale of random peer audits, finds flooding the market far costlier than any profit it could steal.
